F-1_openai_model_lineup.summary: The OpenAI flagship line on 2026-09-16 is gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna. None of the eight models PS-2026-09-15 recorded is a flagship model any more, but ALL EIGHT are still listed on the page, in the collapsed "All models" section.
F-1_openai_model_lineup.price_changes_since_PS-2026-09-15: None. Every one of the eight input and output rates in PS-2026-09-15 still matches the page. What PS-2026-09-15 got wrong was completeness, not the numbers: it omitted the cached-input column that was there all along.
F-1_openai_model_lineup.material_consequence: A run plan naming gpt-5 or gpt-5-mini is still priceable, but it is no longer pricing a current-generation model, and the C4 tier-adjacent pairs in METHODOLOGY section 8 were chosen against a lineup that has moved.

F-2_anthropic_tokenizer_change.summary: Anthropic token counts are NOT comparable across Claude model generations.
F-2_anthropic_tokenizer_change.quoted_evidence: [https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing] "Claude 4.7 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview use a newer tokenizer that contributes to their improved performance on a wide range of tasks. This tokenizer produces approximately 30% more tokens for the same text. The exact increase depends on the content and workload shape. Claude Sonnet 4.6 and earlier models use the previous tokenizer."
F-2_anthropic_tokenizer_change.material_consequence: METHODOLOGY v1.1.0 section 5.1 'Comparability constraint' requires that the only permitted difference between a treatment attempt and its baseline attempt is the registered intervention. A C4 pair that puts Claude Haiku 4.5 (previous tokenizer) against Claude Opus 5 or Sonnet 5 (newer tokenizer) violates it for TOKEN counts: the same text yields ~30% more tokens on one side of the pair for reasons that have nothing to do with the intervention. Section 12 already forbids reporting cross-provider token deltas where accounting is not like-for-like; this finding extends that prohibition WITHIN Anthropic, across the 4.6/4.7 tokenizer boundary. Cost and cost-per-successful-task remain reportable; a token-count delta across that boundary is not.

F-3_meter_assumes_cached_inside_input.summary: environment/harness/meter.py raises MeterError when cached_tokens > input_tokens, with the message "the provider is not reporting these as disjoint". That check encodes the OpenAI/DeepSeek convention, in which cached tokens are INSIDE input_tokens. It is wrong for Anthropic, where total_input_tokens = cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + input_tokens and a cache-heavy call legitimately reports cache_read_input_tokens far larger than input_tokens.
F-3_meter_assumes_cached_inside_input.material_consequence: An Anthropic attempt with a large cached prefix would either raise MeterError or, if the adapter folds the fields together to avoid it, be mispriced. The per-model token_inclusion block in this snapshot records the difference; the meter must read it rather than assume one convention. Raised here as an evidence finding, not fixed -- the meter is not this seat's to change.

cache_ttl.evidence: [https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing] "Prompt caching uses the following pricing multipliers relative to base input token rates: | Cache operation | Multiplier | Duration | | 5-minute cache write | 1.25x base input price | Cache valid for 5 minutes | | 1-hour cache write | 2x base input price | Cache valid for 1 hour |" -- the TTL tier is priced THROUGH the cache-write rate, not as a separate charge. This entry fixes one TTL tier in `plan` and carries that tier's write rate in rates.cache_write, so there is no residual TTL dimension to bill.

other_fees.evidence: [https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing] "Client-side tools are priced the same as any other Claude API request, although server-side tools can incur additional charges based on their specific usage." SCOPE: this entry prices Messages API text-token usage with client-side tools only, which is what Lab 001 workloads A-E use (workload D drives a locally hosted MCP toolset, tasks/TASK_SET_v1.0.0/corpora/mcp_toolset/server.py). Anthropic server-side tools ARE separately billed on the same page -- "Web search is available on the Claude API for $10 per 1,000 searches"; "Additional usage beyond 1,550 hours is billed at $0.05 USD per hour, per container" -- and an attempt that enables one is NOT priced by this entry and is unpriceable under METHODOLOGY v1.1.0 section 11.4.

cached_tokens_in_input.evidence: [https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching] "The usage response includes three separate input token fields that together represent your total input: total_input_tokens = cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + input_tokens" and "Important: input_tokens does NOT represent all input tokens - only the portion after your last cache breakpoint." Cached tokens are therefore ADDITIONAL to the reported input_tokens, not inside it.

reasoning_tokens_in_output.evidence: [https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/extended-thinking] "To track what a budget actually costs you, monitor the usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens field in the response, which reports how many of the billed output tokens were internal reasoning." Thinking tokens are a subset of the billed output_tokens, i.e. already included.

reports_total.evidence: [https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching] The FAQ entry "How do I calculate total input tokens from the usage fields?" answers with a formula the caller must apply -- "total_input_tokens = cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + input_tokens" -- and every usage block published on https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing (e.g. {"input_tokens": 105, "output_tokens": 6039, "cache_read_input_tokens": 7123, "cache_creation_input_tokens": 7345}}) carries no total field. The Messages API does not report a total; the meter must sum the parts.
